title: Jamie and To-do List
statementMd:
*Why I have to finish so many assignments???*

Jamie is getting very busy with his school life. He starts to forget the assignments that he has to do. He decided to write the things down on a to-do list. He assigns a value `priority` for each of his assignment **(lower value means more important)** so he can decide which he needs to spend more time on.

After a few days, Jamie finds out the list is too large that he can't even manage the list by himself! As you are a good friend of Jamie, help him write a program to support the following operations on the to-do list:

- $*set* *a*_{*i*} *x*_{*i*}$ — Add assignment $*a*_{*i*}$ to the to-do list if it is not present, and set its `priority` to $*x*_{*i*}$. If assignment $*a*_{*i*}$ is already in the to-do list, its `priority` **is changed** to $*x*_{*i*}$.
- $*remove* *a*_{*i*}$ — Remove assignment $*a*_{*i*}$ from the to-do list if it is present in it.
- $*query* *a*_{*i*}$ — Output the number of assignments that are more important (have a **smaller** `priority` value) than assignment $*a*_{*i*}$, so Jamie can decide a better schedule. Output $- 1$ if $*a*_{*i*}$ is not in the to-do list.
- $*undo* *d*_{*i*}$ — Undo all changes that have been made in the previous $*d*_{*i*}$ days (not including the day of this operation)

At day $0$, the to-do list is empty. In each of the following $*q*$ days, Jamie will do **exactly one** out of the four operations. If the operation is a $*query*$, you should **output the result of the query before proceeding to the next day**, or poor Jamie cannot make appropriate decisions.

## Input

The first line consists of a single integer $*q*$ $(1 ≤ *q* ≤ 10^{5})$ — the number of operations.

The following $*q*$ lines consists of the description of the operations. The $*i*$-th line consists of the operation that Jamie has done in the $*i*$-th day. The query has the following format:

The first word in the line indicates the type of operation. It must be one of the following four: `set`, `remove`, `query`, `undo`.

- If it is a `set` operation, a string $*a*_{*i*}$ and an integer $*x*_{*i*}$ follows $(1 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$. $*a*_{*i*}$ is the assignment that need to be set to `priority` $*x*_{*i*}$.
- If it is a `remove` operation, a string $*a*_{*i*}$ follows. $*a*_{*i*}$ is the assignment that need to be removed.
- If it is a `query` operation, a string $*a*_{*i*}$ follows. $*a*_{*i*}$ is the assignment that needs to be queried.
- If it is a `undo` operation, an integer $*d*_{*i*}$ follows $(0 ≤ *d*_{*i*} < *i*)$. $*d*_{*i*}$ is the number of days that changes needed to be undone.

All assignment names $*a*_{*i*}$ only consists of lowercase English letters and have a length $1 ≤ |*a*_{*i*}| ≤ 15$.

It is guaranteed that the last operation is a `query` operation.

## Output

For each `query` operation, output a single integer — the number of assignments that have a priority lower than assignment $*a*_{*i*}$, or $- 1$ if $*a*_{*i*}$ is not in the to-do list.

## Interaction

If the operation is a $*query*$, you **should** output the result of the query and flush the output stream before proceeding to the next operation. Otherwise, you may get the verdict `Idleness Limit Exceed`.

For flushing the output stream, please refer to the documentation of your chosen programming language. The flush functions of some common programming languages are listed below:

- C: `fflush(stdout);`
- C++: `cout « flush;`
- Java: `System.out.flush();`
statementZhMd:
*为什么我必须完成这么多作业？？？*

Jamie 的校园生活变得越来越忙碌。他开始忘记自己需要完成的作业，于是决定把这些事情写在待办清单上。他为每项作业指定一个 `priority` 值**（值越小表示越重要）**，这样就能决定哪些作业需要投入更多时间。

几天后，Jamie 发现清单太长了，甚至无法独自管理！作为 Jamie 的好朋友，请你编写一个程序，支持对待办清单进行以下操作：

- $*set* *a*_{*i*} *x*_{*i*}$ — 如果作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 不在待办清单中，则将其加入，并将其 `priority` 设置为 $*x*_{*i*}$。如果作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 已经在待办清单中，则将其 `priority` **修改**为 $*x*_{*i*}$。
- $*remove* *a*_{*i*}$ — 如果作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 在待办清单中，则将其移除。
- $*query* *a*_{*i*}$ — 输出比作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 更重要（具有**更小的** `priority` 值）的作业数量，以便 Jamie 制定更好的计划。如果作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 不在待办清单中，则输出 $- 1$。
- $*undo* *d*_{*i*}$ — 撤销前 $*d*_{*i*}$ 天内进行的所有修改（不包括执行该操作的当天）。

在第 $0$ 天，待办清单为空。在接下来的 $*q*$ 天中，Jamie 每天会恰好执行四种操作中的一种。如果执行的是 $*query*$ 操作，你应当**在进入下一天之前输出查询结果**，否则可怜的 Jamie 将无法做出适当的安排。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*q*$ $(1 ≤ *q* ≤ 10^{5})$ — 操作的数量。

接下来的 $*q*$ 行描述这些操作。第 $*i*$ 行描述 Jamie 在第 $*i*$ 天执行的操作。操作格式如下：

每行的第一个单词表示操作类型，必须是以下四种之一：`set`、`remove`、`query`、`undo`。

- 如果是 `set` 操作，随后会给出一个字符串 $*a*_{*i*}$ 和一个整数 $*x*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$。$*a*_{*i*}$ 是需要将 `priority` 设置为 $*x*_{*i*}$ 的作业。
- 如果是 `remove` 操作，随后会给出一个字符串 $*a*_{*i*}$。$*a*_{*i*}$ 是需要移除的作业。
- 如果是 `query` 操作，随后会给出一个字符串 $*a*_{*i*}$。$*a*_{*i*}$ 是需要查询的作业。
- 如果是 `undo` 操作，随后会给出一个整数 $*d*_{*i*}$ $(0 ≤ *d*_{*i*} < *i*)$。$*d*_{*i*}$ 表示需要撤销修改的天数。

所有作业名称 $*a*_{*i*}$ 仅由小写英文字母组成，长度满足 $1 ≤ |*a*_{*i*}| ≤ 15$。

保证最后一个操作是 `query` 操作。

## 输出格式

对于每个 `query` 操作，输出一个整数 — 具有比作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 更低优先级的作业数量；如果作业 $*a*_{*i*}$ 不在待办清单中，则输出 $- 1$。

## 交互

如果操作是 $*query*$，你**应当输出查询结果，并在进行下一次操作前刷新输出流**。否则，可能会得到 `Idleness Limit Exceed` 的评测结果。

关于如何刷新输出流，请参考所选编程语言的文档。下面列出了一些常见编程语言的刷新函数：

- C：`fflush(stdout);`
- C++：`cout « flush;`
- Java：`System.out.flush();`
